extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator (early-18th-century London literate public)
extracted.subtask_short: spectator essays on clubs and masquerades
extracted.subtask_description: Periodical-essay commentary (The Spectator) describing social institutions (clubs, masquerades), their rules, membership tests, and moral evaluation of their purposes. Includes transcribed rules of a artisans' 'Two-penny Club'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of the Midnight Masque
rubrics_metrics.description: The Women either come by themselves, or are introduced by Friends, who are obliged to quit them upon their first Entrance, to the Conversation of any Body that addresses himself to them. There are several Rooms where the Parties may retire, and, if they please, show their Faces by Consent. Whispers, Squeezes, Nods, and Embraces, are the innocent Freedoms of the Place. In short, the whole Design of this libidinous Assembly seems to terminate in Assignations and Intrigues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masqued anonymity and large numbers protect participants from ordinary social sanction; the narrator regards these practices as tending to immorality and recommends public admonition to prevent such clandestine meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fat-Men Club entrance test
rubrics_metrics.description: A candidate for the corpulent club who could make his Entrance through a moderate-sized door was looked upon as unqualified; but if he stuck in the Passage, and could not force his Way through it, the Folding-Doors were immediately thrown open for his Reception, and he was saluted as a Brother.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership criterion based on a humorous physical test (displaying corpulence); used as an example of arbitrary, characteristic membership rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Scare-Crows and Skeletons' opposing faction
rubrics_metrics.description: A rival club of meagre and envious members ('Scare-Crows and Skeletons') arose to thwart the designs of the Fat-Men and represented them as men of dangerous principles, eventually working them out of favour and the magistracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates how factional club politics can affect municipal governance; a warning about clubs formed from opposition rather than sociability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Kings' confederacy membership by surname
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Kings' Confederacy admitted men of all qualities and professions provided they agreed in this Sir-name of 'King', which they imagined sufficiently declared them untainted with Republican principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership based on nominal badge (surname) rather than merit or belief; example of symbolic or frivolous admission criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Georges' badge-of-distinction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A Christian Name has been used as a Badge of Distinction: That of the 'Georges', who used to meet at the Sign of the 'George', on St. 'George's' day, and swear 'Before George'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of clubs forming around a shared name/celebration and ritual oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Street-Club practice and local control
rubrics_metrics.description: In several parts of the city 'Street-Clubs' exist where chief inhabitants of the street converse together every night; such clubs may take vacant houses into their own hands to control future tenancy and keep the neighbourhood sociable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs used as instruments of local social regulation (including informal market control of rents/tenants).

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Hum-Drum' and 'Mum' clubs: character criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Hum-Drum' Club was made up of very honest gentlemen of peaceable dispositions that used to sit together, smoke their pipes, and say nothing 'till Midnight. The 'Mum' Club is of the same nature and an enemy to Noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines a type of club whose membership is characterized by quiet sociability; suggests that club purpose shapes acceptable member behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club of Duellists admission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Club of Duellists' admitted none that had not fought his Man; the President was said to have killed half a dozen in single Combat, members took their seats according to the number of their slain, and there was a Side-Table for such as had only drawn Blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership based on having committed a specific violent act; satirical illustration of extreme honor-based admission rules and their consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern celebrated clubs founded on eating and drinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Modern celebrated Clubs are founded upon Eating and Drinking, which are Points wherein most Men agree. The 'Kit-Cat' itself is said to have taken its Original from a Mutton-Pye. The 'Beef-Steak' and 'October' Clubs are neither averse to Eating and Drinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical common-ground criterion for many enduring clubs: shared meals and convivial drinking as the basis for association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper purpose of clubs (normative criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When Men are thus knit together by Love of Society, not a Spirit of Faction, and do not meet to censure or annoy those that are absent, but to enjoy one another: when they are combined for their own Improvement, or for the Good of others, or at least to relax themselves from the Business of the Day by an innocent and cheerful Conversation, there may be something very useful in these little Institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative standard for evaluating clubs: beneficial when formed for improvement, mutual enjoyment, and innocent relaxation rather than faction or malice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule I
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Member at his first coming in shall lay down his Two Pence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the enacted 'RULES to be observed in the Two-penny Club' — a subscription/dues rule to fund the club.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule II
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Member shall fill his Pipe out of his own Box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct rule specifying personal responsibility for pipe tobacco (prevents communal depletion/arguments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule III
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member absents himself he shall forfeit a Penny for the Use of the Club, unless in case of Sickness or Imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance/penalty rule to encourage regular participation; allowances for genuine incapacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule IV
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member swears or curses, his Neighbour may give him a Kick upon the Shins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioural enforcement: corporal-but-humorous penalty for coarse language; social enforcement delegated to peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule V
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member tells Stories in the Club that are not true, he shall forfeit for every third Lie an Half-Penny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truthfulness rule with escalating penalty to discourage habitual lying in conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule VI
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member strikes another wrongfully, he shall pay his Club for him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restitution rule for unjustified violence: the offender compensates the club (presumably for costs or fines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule VII
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member brings his Wife into the Club, he shall pay for whatever she drinks or smoaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge rule for guests (wives) to prevent freeloading on club provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule VIII
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member's Wife comes to fetch him Home from the Club, she shall speak to him without the Door.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy/decorum rule regarding interactions with spouses to avoid disturbance inside the club.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule IX
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member calls another Cuckold, he shall be turned out of the Club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defamation/insult rule protecting reputation and prohibiting slanderous accusations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule X
rubrics_metrics.description: None shall be admitted into the Club that is of the same Trade with any Member of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule to prevent trade competition or collusion within the club; ensures diversity of trades among members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule XI
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the Club shall have his Cloaths or Shoes made or mended, but by a Brother Member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutual-support rule reserving paid artisan work to fellow members; fosters internal economy and patronage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club rule XII
rubrics_metrics.description: No Non-juror shall be capable of being a Member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political/religious loyalty qualification (exclusion of 'Non-jurors'); rule reflecting broader civic/political tests for membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club overall purpose and moral
rubrics_metrics.description: These Laws were enacted by a Knot of Artizans and Mechanicks, for the Preservation of Friendship and good Neighbourhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The set is presented as a picture of low life and as a wholesome set of laws and penalties; compared to Ben Johnson's 'Leges Convivales' and ancient club regulations — offered as a model of local moral order.
